2.text: Chukchee on the Arctic shore, 1600, which should be increased to 2000,

3.text: because I omitted in my enumeration some of the minor settlements the names

4.text: of which I obtained, but which I was unable to identify with villages mentioned

5.text: by Lieut. Nordquist. Lieut. Nordquist arrives at the same number of inhabitants,

6.text: but the number of houses in his list are more than 400, as compared with

7.text: 266 enumerated by me. His estimate is based, according to his own statement,

8.text: on the assumption of only five persons to a house, whereas my figure is six

9.text: and a half. With an equal average of inmates to a house, his census of the

10.text: population on the Arctic shores would exceed mine by 600. It seems probable,

11.text: therefore, as Mr. Gondatti asserts, that the maritime population has diminished

12.text: of late years. His assumption, however, that the Arctic shore is more thickly

13.text: populated than the Pacific, seems to me unfounded.

14.text: The total number of the Chukchee amounts to 12,000, rather more than

15.text: less, of which three fourths are reindeer-breeders, and only one fourth maritime.

16.text: The decrease in the maritime population may be partly accounted for by the

17.text: fact that each year many families turn from maritime pursuits to reindeer-

19.text: Several villages have nearly or altogether disappeared, because all the

20.text: inhabitants have gone inland and have turned reindeer-breeders. These are,

21.text: on the Arctic coast, besides those of Kuluˊči Bay, mentioned above, the
